procedural_matters: CHN 365 was represented by Handa Qiao.
NED 174 was represented by Aniek Hill.
R. Valvenbung (team manager NED 174) and Aupas Likel (Coach CHN 365) attended the hearing as observers.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
During the hearing the panel clarified in accordance with RRS 63.2(c) that the hearing request was not only a protest but also a request for redress and proceeded with it accordingly.
facts: The incident occurred approximately half way up the second beat in race 9.
Conditions at the time of the incident: 12-15 knots with slight sea.
CHN 365 was sailing on starboard tack on a close-hauled course.
NED 174 was on port two boat lengths lateral distance away from CHN 365, and aiming approximately three boat lengths in front of CHN 365's bows.
Contact occurred between NED 174's port hull and the stern of CHN 365's port hull.
Damage occurred to CHN 365 in the form of a crack in her hull in front of the rear cross beam, resulting in water ingress.
Damage occurred to NED 174 in the form of a crack in the port bow of approximately 2/3 of the height of the hull, with water ingress.
Both boats retired from the race and did not sail races 10, 11 and 12.
conclusions: NED 174 on port tack failed to keep clear of CHN 365 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
NED 174 did not avoid contact with CHN 365 when it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for CHN 365, the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with NED 174 when it became clear that NED 174 was not keeping clear. CHN 365 did not break RRS 14(a).

CHN 365's scores in races 9, 10, 11 and 12 were made significantly worse through no fault of her own by physical damage because of the action of NED 174 that was breaking RRS 10 and 14 and took an applicable penalty. Therefore, the requirements of rule 61.4(b)(2) are met.
decision: The protest is upheld. Since NED 174 took the applicable penalty, she is not further penalized under RRS 60.5(c)(2).

Redress is given to CHN 365. She is to be scored in races 9, 10, 11, and 12 points equal to the average, rounded to the nearest tenth of a point (0.05 to be rounded upward), of her points in all races sailed before the last scheduled day of the regatta if racing is later scheduled on that day, except races 9,10, 11 and 12. No other boat’s score shall change.
